newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian economic gloom hit Nestle profit.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian economic gloom hit Nestle profit.

text.p: A fall in first quarter profits at leading Nigerian food company Nestle on Monday shocked the stock market but traders took it in their stride as Nestle blamed the situation on the country's economic recession.
The company said profit after tax in the quarter to end-March 1997 fell to 101.2 million naira ($1.2 million) from 112.1 million naira in the same period last year.
Two months ago, Nestle announced an excellent full year 1996 account in which profits doubled from 1995, making its stock the most bullish on the Nigerian bourse since then.
"The market is naturally disappointed but it does not mean the shares would go on offer," one trader said.
Nestle shares were steady at 52.30 naira on Monday.

In a statement to stock dealers, the company blamed the lower profit on the general economic situation in Nigeria, adding that lack of liquidity in the nation hit consumers' disposable income during the period.
Traders gave a similar reason for the 20 percent drop in first quarter profits at Nigerian Breweries last week.
Tyre maker Dunlop, which also announced its first quarter results on Monday, brought more cheer to the market.
It posted a slightly higher after-tax profit of 83.2 million naira for the period to end-March 1997 from 70.6 million in the comparable 1996 period.
Traders attributed this to recent reorganisation it carried out to cut costs, including a reduction in the workforce.

Nestle became the hottest stock on the Nigerian stock market on May 5 when it posted an after-tax profit of 1.2 billion naira in 1996 against 612.8 million naira a year earlier, a six naira dividend per share and a one-for-one scrip issue.
Its shares have consistently climbed on persistent demand.
Traders said they did not expect demand to wane but that they would be more cautious in their pricing of the stock.
Most Nigerian manufacturers have been reporting poorer results in the face of high operating costs coupled with low demand.
Analysts said a crippling fuel scarcity which is now abating due to importation of petroleum products was likely to worsen the financial position of manufacturers this year.
"Many companies can't guarantee a stable production run," one said. "A worsening story will unfold by the time we see first quarter and half year results," he added.
Nestle products include Maggi soup and stew seasonings, noodles, cereals and Milo food drink.
Nestle S.A. of Switzerland owns at least 50 percent of shares in the company while Nigerians hold the rest.
